title: About the course
tagline: Reading, understanding and analysing corporate financial statements.
facts: Accounting and Finance, University of Valladolid

sections.heading: What the course is about
paras: Financial Statement Analysis gives you the tools to understand a company's current financial position and to build forward-looking projections for managerial decisions — its asset, financial and economic situation, its internal structure, its strengths and weaknesses, and the external constraints it faces.

The course introduces the main techniques for analysing companies from external accounting information. It is a discipline rooted in accounting: progress depends directly on a solid grasp of the basic accounting concepts. It is also interdisciplinary, drawing on taxation, law, business strategy and, above all, corporate finance.

sections.heading: By the end of the course you should be able to
list: Identify the main sources of financial information.
Understand and analyse corporate financial statements.
Prepare reports on a company's economic and financial situation.

sections.heading: Contents
list: 2 — Financial statements I: balance sheet and income statement
3 — Financial statements II: statement of changes in equity, cash flow statement and notes
5 — Economic and financial analysis I: profitability
6 — Economic and financial analysis II: liquidity, solvency and growth

sections.heading: How the course is taught
list: Practical sessions solving exercises and case studies — to be attempted before class.
Individual and group assignments analysing real companies, with written reports on their financial situation and profitability.

sections.heading: Assessment
paras: Continuous assessment (active participation and written tests during the term): up to 30%, worth up to 3 points. These points are added to the final exam only if the final written exam scores at least 5 out of 10.
Final written exam: two parts, one theoretical and one with practical case studies. Up to 70% under continuous assessment, or 100% otherwise.
Resit (extraordinary session): a single final written exam covering theory and case studies, 100% of the grade.

sections.heading: Workload — 6 ECTS, 150 h
list: Face-to-face (60 h): 30 h lectures, 26 h practical classes, 4 h assessment and other activities.
Independent work (90 h): 80 h individual study, 10 h group work.

sections.heading: Main references
list: Weygandt, Kimmel & Mitchell — Financial Accounting, 12th ed., Wiley, 2023.
Horngren — Introduction to Financial Accounting, 11th ed., Pearson, 2014.
Horngren, Harrison & Bamber — Financial Accounting, 5th ed., Pearson, 2003.

note: Summary based on the official course syllabus (guía docente) approved by the Degree Committee. The version published on the UVa website is the authoritative one.
